# burigangaamr

<!-- badges: start -->

[![License: CC BY
4.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-CC_BY_4.0-lightgrey.svg)](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/openwashdata/burigangaamr/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/openwashdata/burigangaamr/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)

<!-- badges: end -->

The goal of burigangaamr is to provide the antibiotic susceptibility test
results of 50 *Pseudomonas aeruginosa* isolates from surface water at seven
sites along the Buriganga River, Bangladesh, sampled from March to May
2023, as tidy data. The isolates were
tested against nine antibiotics with the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method.
The data are republished from the supplementary tables of Sharif, Amin,
Mehbub and Ratul (2024), published under CC BY 4.0 in the Journal of Water
and Health (see Source and changes below).

**Draft.** This package is not released, has no DOI and may still change.
The original authors will be notified before the first release.

## Installation

You can install the development version of burigangaamr from
[GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("openwashdata/burigangaamr")
```

```{r}
## Run the following code in console if you don't have the packages
## install.packages(c("dplyr", "knitr", "readr", "stringr", "gt", "kableExtra"))
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(readr)
library(stringr)
library(gt)
library(kableExtra)
```

Alternatively, you can download the individual datasets as a CSV or XLSX
file from the table below.

1.  Click Download CSV. A window opens that displays the CSV in
    your browser.
2.  Right-click anywhere inside the window and select "Save Page As...".
3.  Save the file in a folder of your choice.

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

extdata_path <- "https://github.com/openwashdata/burigangaamr/raw/main/inst/extdata/"

read_csv("data-raw/dictionary.csv") |> 
  distinct(file_name) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(file_name = str_remove(file_name, ".rda")) |> 
  dplyr::rename(dataset = file_name) |> 
  mutate(
    CSV = paste0("[Download CSV](", extdata_path, dataset, ".csv)"),
    XLSX = paste0("[Download XLSX](", extdata_path, dataset, ".xlsx)")
  ) |> 
  knitr::kable()

```

## Data

The package provides access to three data objects. `burigangaamr` holds one
row per isolate and antibiotic, `burigangaamr_isolates` one row per isolate,
and `burigangaamr_antibiotics` one row per antibiotic with the breakpoints
used to interpret the zone diameters.

```{r}
library(burigangaamr)
```

### burigangaamr

The dataset `burigangaamr` contains the zone diameter and its interpretation
(susceptible, intermediate or resistant) for every isolate and antibiotic.
It has `r nrow(burigangaamr)` observations and `r ncol(burigangaamr)`
variables

```{r}
burigangaamr |> 
  head(3) |> 
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::as_raw_html()
```

For an overview of the variable names, see the following table.

```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
readr::read_csv("data-raw/dictionary.csv") |>
  dplyr::filter(file_name == "burigangaamr.rda") |>
  dplyr::select(variable_name:description) |> 
  knitr::kable() |> 
  kableExtra::kable_styling("striped") |> 
  kableExtra::scroll_box(height = "200px")
```

### burigangaamr_isolates

The dataset `burigangaamr_isolates` contains one row per isolate with the
number of resistant and intermediate results, the number of antibiotic
classes with resistance, the antibiotics listed as nonsusceptible in the
supplement and the multidrug resistance flag. It has
`r nrow(burigangaamr_isolates)` observations and
`r ncol(burigangaamr_isolates)` variables

```{r}
burigangaamr_isolates |> 
  head(3) |> 
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::as_raw_html()
```

For an overview of the variable names, see the following table.

```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
readr::read_csv("data-raw/dictionary.csv") |>
  dplyr::filter(file_name == "burigangaamr_isolates.rda") |>
  dplyr::select(variable_name:description) |> 
  knitr::kable() |> 
  kableExtra::kable_styling("striped") |> 
  kableExtra::scroll_box(height = "200px")
```

### burigangaamr_antibiotics

The dataset `burigangaamr_antibiotics` contains the nine antibiotics with
their class, the disc content and the zone diameter breakpoints for
resistant, intermediate and susceptible. It has
`r nrow(burigangaamr_antibiotics)` observations and
`r ncol(burigangaamr_antibiotics)` variables

```{r}
burigangaamr_antibiotics |> 
  head(3) |> 
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::as_raw_html()
```

For an overview of the variable names, see the following table.

```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
readr::read_csv("data-raw/dictionary.csv") |>
  dplyr::filter(file_name == "burigangaamr_antibiotics.rda") |>
  dplyr::select(variable_name:description) |> 
  knitr::kable() |> 
  kableExtra::kable_styling("striped") |> 
  kableExtra::scroll_box(height = "200px")
```

## Example

The figure `resistance-shares` shows, for each antibiotic, the share of
the 50 isolates that tested susceptible, intermediate or resistant. Resistance is concentrated in
cefotaxime and tetracycline, where 88 percent of the isolates were
resistant, while every isolate was susceptible to piperacillin-tazobactam.

```{r resistance-shares, fig.alt="Horizontal stacked bar chart of the share of the 50 isolates that tested susceptible, intermediate or resistant to each of the nine antibiotics, ordered from the lowest to the highest share resistant"}
library(burigangaamr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

shares <- burigangaamr |>
  count(antibiotic, interpretation) |>
  group_by(antibiotic) |>
  mutate(share = n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup()

antibiotic_order <- shares |>
  group_by(antibiotic) |>
  summarise(resistant = sum(share[interpretation == "resistant"])) |>
  arrange(resistant) |>
  pull(antibiotic)

shares |>
  mutate(antibiotic = factor(antibiotic, levels = antibiotic_order)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = share, y = antibiotic, fill = interpretation)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent()) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(susceptible = "#5B8E7D",
                               intermediate = "#E1B12C",
                               resistant = "#B5473B")) +
  labs(x = "Share of the 50 isolates", y = NULL, fill = NULL,
       title = "Disc diffusion results per antibiotic") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Source and changes

The data come from the supplementary material of Sharif, D. I., Amin, F.,
Mehbub, M. H. and Ratul, R. I. (2024). Distribution and antibiotic
resistance patterns of *Pseudomonas aeruginosa* across different point
sources of pollution in the Buriganga River, Bangladesh. *Journal of Water
and Health*, 22(12). <https://doi.org/10.2166/wh.2024.270>. The article and
its supplement are published under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0
licence. The original authors are listed in the package as data
contributors; they have not reviewed this package.

We changed the material. The eight Word tables of the supplement were read
into R (the script is in `data-raw/data_processing.R`). The two isolate by
antibiotic matrices (zone diameters in table S3, interpretations in table
S4) were reshaped into one observation per isolate and antibiotic, the
antibiotic codes were expanded with names, classes and disc contents from
tables S1 and S2, the breakpoints of table S2 were split into numbers, and
the counts per isolate were derived from the observations. Tables S5, S7
and S8 are summaries and are not republished; the processing script
reproduces every percentage of S5 and S8 from the data.

Two statements of the supplement and the article do not agree with each
other, and the package keeps the supplement as it is:

- Table S6 flags 14 isolates as multidrug resistant, while table S7 and the
  abstract count 13. The difference is isolate B1c, which is resistant to
  two antibiotic classes.
- The abstract reports that 4 percent of the isolates (two) were resistant
  to both imipenem and meropenem; in table S4 one isolate is.
- Table S6 lists ciprofloxacin (CIP) among the nonsusceptible antibiotics
  of isolate G3a, while tables S3 and S4 record a 35 mm zone and a
  susceptible result for ciprofloxacin and a resistant result for
  cefotaxime (CTX) instead. The counts per isolate come from tables S3
  and S4; the listed codes come from table S6.

Surface water was sampled from 1 March to 15 May 2023, in the pre-monsoon
season, at seven points along the river between Sadar Ghat and Midford
Ghat, each chosen for a nearby source of pollution (article, Methods and
Table 2); 70 *P. aeruginosa* isolates were obtained and 50 of them were
tested against the nine antibiotics. The site descriptions of Table 2 are
in the dictionary under `site`.
